question: Why do we do a ward orientation for a brand-new patient?

options.A: To tick the box for hospital accreditation
options.B: To help them feel at home and less anxious
options.C: To check their memory and brain function
options.D: To keep them busy while doctors do paperwork

explanation: You've got this! Showing a new patient around—like pointing out the call bell and toilet—makes them feel safe and lowers that scary hospital anxiety. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the best way to handle a new patient's expensive things when they arrive on the ward?

options.A: Record and secure them following your hospital's property policy
options.B: Tell them to keep everything stuffed in their bedside drawer
options.C: Leave them on the nurse's desk without writing anything down
options.D: Throw them away so the ward stays tidy

explanation: Smart nursing! Cataloging and locking away valuables protects both the patient from theft and you from any blame if something goes missing. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: What kind of hospital admission is planned well ahead of time for a surgery?
explanation: Spot on! Routine admissions are planned in advance, giving the team time to prep the bed and tests before the patient even shows up. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient is rushed into the ward unconscious after a terrible road crash. What type of admission is this?
explanation: Correct! Sudden accidents and severe illnesses need unplanned, immediate care, which we call an emergency admission. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is keeping accurate notes during admission so important legally?

options.A: It handles the insurance billing without needing clinical details
options.B: It lets family members read private nurse notes anytime
options.C: It helps meet the hospital management's money targets
options.D: It serves as proof of the care you gave if there's ever a legal issue

explanation: You nailed it. Your nursing notes are legal evidence of what assessments and care you performed for that patient. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is it a bad idea to wait until the end of your shift to record vital signs?

options.A: It always gets your nursing license cancelled immediately
options.B: It makes the patient's chart look messy
options.C: It breaks the decoration rules at the nurse's station
options.D: You might forget important details and put the patient at risk

explanation: Always document promptly! Writing things down right away means any dangerous changes are caught and reported fast. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: When does a hospital need to refer a patient to another facility?

options.A: When the patient's family refuses to pay the deposit
options.B: When the nurse wants a long annual leave
options.C: When the patient complains about the ward food
options.D: When the hospital lacks the right tools or specialists to help them

explanation: Exactly! If your center can't provide the specialized care they need, referring them up is the safest and best choice. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: You need to rush an unstable patient to a bigger hospital. What is the most important thing to do?

options.A: Wait till morning shift to send their file
options.B: Ask the relatives to carry the treatment chart themselves
options.C: Let the patient walk to the ambulance to save battery power
options.D: Send an escort nurse with emergency supplies and proper referral notes

explanation: Great thinking! Unstable patients need a nurse watching them with supplies on hand, plus clear referral notes for the receiving team. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: At what point in a hospital stay should you actually start planning for the patient's discharge?

options.A: When the patient asks for their file
options.B: Right on the day they get admitted
options.C: Two hours before they leave the ward
options.D: During the doctor's final clearance round

explanation: You got it! Starting discharge planning early gives you enough time to sort out home care and teaching before they walk out the door. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do we involve different health professionals when preparing a patient for discharge?

options.A: It brings different experts together to cover all of the patient's home needs
options.B: It means nurses don't have to teach patients anything
options.C: It cuts down the number of empty beds in the ward
options.D: It stops doctors from having to talk to the family

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Physiotherapists, pharmacists, and nurses all share their skills so the patient goes home safely. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: What should you do if a patient insists on leaving the hospital against medical advice (AMA)?

options.A: Document it and have them sign an AMA waiver form
options.B: Ignore them because people have free movement
options.C: Call the police immediately to arrest them
options.D: Lock the ward doors so they can't escape

explanation: Spot on. After counseling them on the risks, having them sign an AMA form covers the hospital legally if they choose to leave early. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is your very first step if you discover a patient has sneaked out and absconded from the ward?

options.A: Alert hospital security and management right away following protocol
options.B: Wait 48 hours to see if they will come back
options.C: Discharge their file like a normal patient
options.D: Pay their hospital bill using your own money

explanation: You're doing great! An abscondment needs immediate reporting to security and management to ensure the patient's safety and protect the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)
